scope: pcs-backend P7 Sprint 4 (base 3e5ae90, head cae5bce), non-test production files

findings.title: Dead module-level index: `_RULE_INDEX` is built once and never read
findings.why_it_matters: `_RULE_INDEX` is constructed at import time and no code in the repo reads it — `find_rule` deliberately walks `SPEC_RULES` linearly and matches on normalized names plus aliases, so a dict keyed by raw `parameter` could not serve it anyway. A future maintainer who sees the index will assume lookup is by exact parameter name and may build on it, or 'optimize' `find_rule` to use it and silently break alias matching for every parameter whose display name differs from its canonical one (扬程/效率/NPSHr all have aliases). It also builds a 7-entry dict on every import for no benefit.
evidence: app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:166 — `_RULE_INDEX = {r.parameter: r for r in SPEC_RULES}`
app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:169-174 — `find_rule` iterates `SPEC_RULES` and calls `rule.matches(name)`; it never references `_RULE_INDEX`
repo-wide grep for `_RULE_INDEX` returns exactly one hit: its own definition
findings.suggested_fix: Delete line 166. If a name->rule lookup is ever genuinely needed, key it on the normalized name AND all normalized aliases (`_normalize` already exists), not on `r.parameter` alone — otherwise it will not be a drop-in for `find_rule`.

findings.title: Dead helper `_cell()` — a Pass-Through Method with zero callers
findings.why_it_matters: `_cell(container, row)` ignores both of its parameters' semantics and returns `asdict(row)` — the `container` argument is never read, and the local `from dataclasses import asdict` inside the function body is the only reason it isn't an unused top-level import. Nothing calls it. It reads like the cell-rendering helper the xlsx exporter once had, which invites a future maintainer to call it expecting row-to-cell formatting and instead get a raw dict, or to 'fix' the unused parameter.
evidence: app/services/supplier/deviation_report.py:189-192 — `def _cell(container, row) -> dict:` / `    from dataclasses import asdict` / `    return asdict(row)`
repo-wide grep for `_cell(` returns no caller (the only other hits are unrelated `test_number_cell` / `test_text_cell` in tests/services/test_worley_extract.py)
findings.suggested_fix: Delete lines 189-192 entirely. If row serialization is genuinely needed, `dataclasses.asdict` is the correct expression at the call site — `export_excel` already writes fields positionally and needs no dict.

findings.title: Stale docstring table contradicts the registry: 电机额定功率 is not SYMMETRIC_BAND, and the SYMMETRIC_BAND branch has no SPEC rule
findings.why_it_matters: The module docstring is the table a maintainer reads before touching anything — it is explicitly framed as the transcription of SPEC §3.2.4(2) and the file header warns 勿凭印象改数值. But row 4 still describes 电机额定功率 as SYMMETRIC_BAND ±10% while the registry entry (line 133) is MOTOR_TIER_FLOOR, and the SYMMETRIC_BAND branch in `evaluate` (line 251) is reachable only from a hand-built `DeviationRule` in `tests/services/supplier/test_deviation_service.py:118`. So a reader trusting the docstring will look for a ±10% band that no longer exists, while a reader of the code sees an unexercised branch in a file whose whole job is to transcribe the SPEC. The correct answer is recorded in the rule's own `spec_ref` (lines 135-139) and in the `_MOTOR_TIER_SMALL_MAX` comment (lines 186-189) — the summary table is the one place that was not updated.
evidence: app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:11 — `| 实际电机额定功率   | 偏差 ±10%               | SYMMETRIC_BAND   | 偏小→不满足，偏大→可接受 |`
app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:132-133 — `        parameter="电机额定功率",` / `        kind="MOTOR_TIER_FLOOR",`
app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:137-138 — `"（**取代** SPEC §3.2.4(2) 原「偏差 ±10%」—— 电机按系列选取, "` — the registry records the supersession, the docstring does not
app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:251 — `    if rule.kind == "SYMMETRIC_BAND":` — no entry in SPEC_RULES (lines 109-164) carries this kind
findings.suggested_fix: Update docstring row 4 to `| 实际电机额定功率 | API 610 分档下限 (轴功率×1.25/1.15/1.10) | MOTOR_TIER_FLOOR | 低于下限→不满足 |` and add the 轴功率 REFERENCE_ONLY row, so the table has 7 rows and matches SPEC_RULES one-for-one. Then decide the SYMMETRIC_BAND branch explicitly: if no SPEC rule can ever be a symmetric band, delete lines 251-256 and the test at test_deviation_service.py:118; if one is coming in a later SPEC revision, leave the branch and add a one-line comment saying it is reserved for a future symmetric-band rule. Assumption: SPEC V1.4 §3.2.4(2) will not add a symmetric-band rule in this sprint — if it will, the second option is correct and the finding downgrades to a docstring-only fix.

findings.title: "已知缺口：design_parameters_json 无写入方" is contradicted by the writer this same diff adds
findings.why_it_matters: Two production modules open with a ⚠️ warning that every report row will fall to 「缺设计值（不可判）」 and `can_confirm` will therefore be permanently False. Commit cae5bce in this same diff range adds exactly the missing writer — `app/services/equip_list/pump_design_data.py::apply_design_parameters` — plus a seed script to invoke it. Leaving the warnings in place means the first thing a maintainer or a code-reading agent does with these files is discount the deviation engine as untestable, and a reviewer of a future change may accept a regression to 「all rows unjudgeable」 as the already-known baseline rather than as new breakage.
evidence: app/services/supplier/deviation_report.py:7-9 — `⚠️ **已知缺口** (2026-10-05 用户裁决「设计值留空」): `design_parameters_json`` / `无写入方，生产路径上所有行都会落到「缺设计值（不可判）」，因而 `can_confirm` 恒` / `False。引擎本身已按 SPEC 逐条实现并由单测覆盖；设计值来源是另一个决定。`
app/api/v1/supplier.py:153-154 — `    ⚠️ 已知缺口：`design_parameters_json` 目前无写入方，故生产路径上全部行` / `    都会落「缺设计值（不可判）」。引擎已按 SPEC 逐条实现，设计值来源待定。`
app/services/equip_list/pump_design_data.py:107-143 — `async def apply_design_parameters(...)` sets `record.design_parameters_json = params` (line 138); this function is new in this diff
findings.suggested_fix: Delete both ⚠️ blocks and replace with the actual current state: design values come from `app/services/equip_list/pump_design_data.py::PUMP_DESIGN` via `apply_design_parameters`, and the residual gap is that PUMP_DESIGN covers only the 18 蜡油加氢 pump tags, so equipment outside that tag set still yields 不可判 rows. If a partial-PUMP_DESIGN warning is wanted, state that one — it is the gap a reader actually needs, and it is a different claim from the one currently written.

findings.title: Repeated Switches: the 4-verdict vocabulary is restated at 6 sites in 3 modules, and 2 of them key on the rendered label string
findings.why_it_matters: Adding a fifth verdict — the obvious next step, and the one this design deliberately invites by making the set open — requires editing the four module constants, `_LABELS`, `_COLORS`, the `Verdict` Literal, `_FILL` and `_FONT_COLOR`, and a missed entry has no error: `_FILL.get(row.label, "FFD9D9D9")` and `verdict_label`'s `.get(verdict, "不可判")` both swallow the miss and render the new verdict as 不可判/gray. Worse, `_FILL` and `_FONT_COLOR` are keyed on the *label* (`"合格"`), not on the verdict constant, so they are coupled to a display string that `_LABELS` owns: editing a label in `_LABELS` silently drops every xlsx/PDF fill to gray while the color column still says 绿色. The PDF path then re-derives hex by string-slicing the openpyxl ARGB (`"#" + argb[2:]`), so the two exporters are coupled through a string format rather than through a shared value.
evidence: app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:28-31 — `QUALIFIED = "QUALIFIED"` / `WARNING = "WARNING"` / `UNQUALIFIED = "UNQUALIFIED"` / `UNVERDICTABLE = "UNVERDICTABLE"` (copy 1)
app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:33-38 — `_LABELS = { QUALIFIED: "合格", WARNING: "警告", UNQUALIFIED: "不合格", UNVERDICTABLE: "不可判" }` (copy 2, keyed by verdict)
app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:41-46 — `_COLORS = { QUALIFIED: "绿色", ... UNVERDICTABLE: "灰色" }` (copy 3, keyed by verdict)
app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:306-311 — `verdict_label` / `verdict_color` both use `.get(verdict, ...)` with a default, so an unknown verdict is silently rendered 不可判/灰色
app/services/supplier/deviation_report.py:171-182 — `_FILL = {"合格": ..., "警告": ..., "不合格": ..., "不可判": ...}` and `_FONT_COLOR = {...}` (copies 4 and 5, keyed by LABEL not verdict)
app/schemas/supplier.py:73 — `Verdict = Literal["QUALIFIED", "WARNING", "UNQUALIFIED", "UNVERDICTABLE"]` (copy 6, in a different module, with no link to copies 1-5)
findings.suggested_fix: Collapse copies 1-5 into one table in deviation_service.py, keyed by the verdict constant: `@dataclass(frozen=True) class VerdictStyle: verdict: str; label: str; color: str; fill: str; font: str` + `VERDICT_STYLES: dict[str, VerdictStyle] = {QUALIFIED: VerdictStyle(QUALIFIED, "合格", "绿色", "FFC6EFCE", "FF006100"), ...}`. `Evaluation.label`/`.color`, `verdict_label`/`verdict_color` and both exporters then read from it; delete `_FILL` and `_FONT_COLOR` from deviation_report.py. Keep the two `.get(..., default)` lookups but change them to raise (or assert) on an unknown verdict so the next addition fails loudly instead of rendering gray. For copy 6, add a one-line test `assert set(VERDICT_STYLES) == set(get_args(Verdict))` in tests/services/supplier/test_deviation_service.py — the Literal cannot be derived at runtime, so a guard test is the cheapest way to keep the two in sync. Keep the ARGB as the single stored format; the existing PDF comment at line 294-295 explaining the slice is worth preserving as the reason.

findings.title: Stale usage example: events.py docstring still tells readers to import from `app.core.events`, the module this diff moved out of `app/core/`
findings.why_it_matters: The move from `app/core/` to `app/services/` is the whole point of this file's diff, and every real caller (cia_engine, confirmation_service, all five test modules) uses the new path. The docstring is the sole remaining `app.core.events` reference in the repo, and it sits inside a `用法::` block written specifically to be copy-pasted — a reader following it gets `ModuleNotFoundError`. The rest of the docstring was carefully updated to describe the new design (deepcopy, DB-backed idempotency); this one line was missed, which is exactly the drift the review persona asks to catch.
evidence: app/services/events.py:22 — `    from app.core.events import emit_event, register_listener`

repo-wide grep for `app.core.events` returns exactly one hit: this docstring line. `app.services.events` is imported by app/services/cia_engine.py:38, app/services/supplier/confirmation_service.py:32, and 4 test modules
findings.suggested_fix: Change line 22 to `from app.services.events import emit_event, register_listener`.

findings.title: build_report constructs the same frozen dataclass twice — the first `report` exists only to be unpacked
findings.why_it_matters: `DeviationReport` is `frozen=True`, so the second construction copies every field verbatim off the first purely to add `blocking_reason`. A maintainer adding a field to `DeviationReport` must add it twice and will eventually add it to only one — the omission is invisible because the second construction is the one that is returned, and the resulting bug is a silently-defaulted field rather than an error.
evidence: app/services/supplier/deviation_report.py:125-130 — `    report = DeviationReport(` / `        equipment_id=str(equipment.equipment_id),` / `        tag_number=equipment.tag_number,` / `        actual_data_status=equipment.actual_data_status,` / `        rows=tuple(rows),` / `    )`

app/services/supplier/deviation_report.py:131-137 — `    return DeviationReport(` repeats equipment_id/tag_number/actual_data_status/rows field-for-field and adds `blocking_reason=_blocking_reason(report.rows),`
findings.suggested_fix: Collapse to a single construction: `return DeviationReport(equipment_id=str(equipment.equipment_id), tag_number=equipment.tag_number, actual_data_status=equipment.actual_data_status, rows=tuple(rows), blocking_reason=_blocking_reason(rows))`. `_blocking_reason` already takes the rows tuple, so the intermediate object is not needed as an argument.

findings.title: The pump-record WHERE clause is duplicated between `apply_design_parameters` and its own seed script
findings.why_it_matters: The script issues its own copy of the exact same query to print a 'before' snapshot, and the two numbers it prints side by side — 「位号匹配 N 台」 and 「写入设计值: M 台」 — read as if M were derived from N, which is only true while the two WHERE clauses match. Any future edit to the filter (adding a project type check, a status check, or a `design_parameters_json IS NULL` guard) updates one copy and leaves the other reporting a stale match count with no error, so the script's output — the only visibility anyone has into this backfill — becomes quietly wrong. The script's purpose is reporting, which makes it the most expensive place for the two to drift.
evidence: app/services/equip_list/pump_design_data.py:124-131 — `    records = (` / `        await session.execute(` / `            select(EquipmentList).where(` / `                EquipmentList.project_id == project_id,` / `                EquipmentList.tag_number.in_(list(PUMP_DESIGN)),` / `            )` / `        )` / `    ).scalars().all()`

scripts/p7_s4_003_seed_pump_design.py:51-58 — `        before = (` / `            await session.execute(` / `                select(EquipmentList).where(` / `                    EquipmentList.project_id == project_id,` / `                    EquipmentList.tag_number.in_(list(PUMP_DESIGN)),` / `                )` / `            )` / `        ).scalars().all()` — byte-for-byte the same predicate
scripts/p7_s4_003_seed_pump_design.py:60 and :63 — the two prints a reader will compare: `位号匹配 {len(before)} 台` / `写入设计值: {n} 台`
findings.suggested_fix: Expose the query once: add `async def matching_pump_records(session, project_id) -> Sequence[EquipmentList]` to pump_design_data.py holding the select, have `apply_design_parameters` call it, and have the script's `_main` call it for its snapshot too. Then the printed count and the written count are provably over the same row set. Assumption: the script's snapshot is genuinely meant to be the same population as the write, not a broader 'what exists in this project' view — if it is meant to be broader, keep both selects but say so in the script's docstring, because the current side-by-side print implies they are the same.

findings.title: Package docstring advertises `excel_import_service`, a module that does not exist and that S4-1 ruled out
findings.why_it_matters: The package docstring indexes its own submodules, so a reader uses it to decide what exists. It names a module that has never existed, and the same design decision is recorded in the opposite direction elsewhere in this diff: `app/api/v1/supplier.py:9-10` states 录入入口是**手工 UI 页面**（S4-1 裁决）：要求供应商填统一 Excel 不现实，故无 Excel 批量导入端点. A maintainer trusting the package docstring will plan the Excel import that the S4-1 ruling explicitly deferred.
evidence: app/services/supplier/__init__.py:3-4 — `- `actual_data_service`: 手动录入供应商实测值` / `- `excel_import_service`: Excel 批量导入`
`ls app/services/supplier/` returns `__init__.py  actual_data_service.py  confirmation_service.py  deviation_report.py  deviation_service.py` — no `excel_import_service.py`
app/api/v1/supplier.py:9-10 — `录入入口是**手工 UI 页面**（S4-1 裁决）：要求供应商填统一 Excel 不现实，` / `故无 Excel 批量导入端点 —— 设备方逐项在页面上录入。`
findings.suggested_fix: Replace line 4 with the three modules that exist and carry the report flow, e.g. `- `confirmation_service`: 确认/校核流程（SPEC §3.2.4(4)）` and `- `deviation_service` / `deviation_report`: 偏差判定与报告（SPEC §3.2.4(2)(3)）`. `actual_data_service` on line 3 is already correct.

findings.title: The parameter-name vocabulary is maintained three times over (rules, design data, units) with no guard against drift
findings.why_it_matters: PUMP_DESIGN's keys, _UNITS' keys, and `DeviationRule.parameter`/`.aliases` are three hand-maintained copies of the same Chinese parameter names, and they only line up by convention. Today they happen to agree, but a rename in one place fails silently: `_UNITS.get(name, "")` yields an empty unit string (which the API schema accepts and the xlsx writes as a blank 单位 column), and `find_rule` returns None so the row is reported 「无判定规则」 rather than erroring. The registry already earns its keep as the canonical list; nothing wires the other two copies to it.
evidence: app/services/equip_list/pump_design_data.py:83-91 — `_UNITS: dict[str, str] = { "扬程": "m", "效率": "-", "NPSHr": "m", "轴功率": "kW", "电机额定功率": "kW", "电机配用功率": "kW", "转速": "r/min" }` — a third hand-maintained name list

app/services/equip_list/pump_design_data.py:38 — `"132-P-101A/B": {"扬程": 2100.0, "效率": 0.8, "NPSHr": 2.0, "轴功率": 2214.06,` ... `"电机额定功率": 2500.0, "电机配用功率": 3300.0, "转速": 2982.0},` — the name list PUMP_DESIGN keys off
app/services/equip_list/pump_design_data.py:101 — `        name: {"value": float(value), "unit": _UNITS.get(name, "")}` — a miss is an empty string, not an error
app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:110-164 — SPEC_RULES is the fourth copy, holding the same names plus aliases
app/services/equip_list/pump_design_data.py:39 — `"电机配用功率": 3300.0` has no `DeviationRule`; a supplier entering that parameter as actual data gets 「无判定规则（SPEC §3.2.4(2) 以泵为例）」
findings.suggested_fix: Cheapest guard that converts silent drift into a test failure, without restructuring the data: in tests/services/equip_list/test_pump_design_data.py add `assert set(_UNITS) == {n for row in PUMP_DESIGN.values() for n in row}` and `assert set(_UNITS) <= {r.parameter for r in SPEC_RULES} | {"电机配用功率"}` — the second assertion makes an intentional non-judged design parameter an explicit, reviewable entry rather than an accident. Assumption: `_UNITS` is intended to stay private; if it is going to be consulted elsewhere, promote it to a module-level public name and let the rule registry import it instead, so the unit table has exactly one owner.

residual_risks: The rule registry (M-context) itself checks out: SPEC_RULES has 7 entries across 7 kinds, all 7 kinds are dispatched in evaluate(), and it has two real production consumers (find_rule from build_report, and the rule constants surfaced into DeviationRow.spec_ref). It is not Speculative Generality and I did not flag it. The flat 8-field DeviationRule is also the smaller concept count than a sum type would be here — 6 of 8 fields are optional, but only design_parameter overrides behaviour (via the design_key property) and the others are plain None-as-absent; a per-kind subclass would add 7 classes to remove 2 `if rule.x is None` reads.

The kind-dispatch in evaluate() (lines 212-272) is a linear if-chain over a string-typed `kind` with a fail-closed default, not a Repeated Switches instance in the Fowler sense — there is exactly one dispatch site for `kind`. The genuine Repeated Switches in this diff is over the *verdict* set, which I filed as M5.

I did not reach a full read of app/models/system.py, app/models/equipment.py, app/api/v1/__init__.py, the two alembic migrations, or the app/services/cia_engine.py diff hunks (line counts were taken via wc, and the git diff --stat call was refused by the worktree guard). The cia_engine import block I did read is correctly layered (services + models only, no app/api import), which supports the intent's claim that the events.py move did not invert the graph — but I verified that for cia_engine only, not for every consumer.

M4's suggested fix rests on the assumption that `apply_design_parameters` is actually wired into a production path (the seed script) and not merely available. If the intended rollout is for the script to be a one-off manual backfill with no automated caller, the ⚠️ warnings are less wrong than I judged them — they would then need rewording to say the values exist only for backfilled projects, not that no writer exists. I graded this P2 rather than P1 for that reason.

Not assessed for maintainability: whether PUMP_DESIGN's 18 transcribed tags and 132-P-105A/B/C/D exclusion are correct transcriptions of the source spreadsheet (that is a correctness/data-provenance question outside this reviewer's remit), and whether the frontend `api.d.ts` snapshot is regenerated in step with the schema change.
testing_gaps: No test asserts that the Verdict Literal in app/schemas/supplier.py:73 matches the constants and maps in app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py — the drift M5 describes would be caught by `assert set(VERDICT_STYLES) == set(get_args(Verdict))`, which does not exist.
No test asserts that _UNITS covers exactly the PUMP_DESIGN key set (M10), so a parameter added to the design table without a unit silently produces an empty 单位 column in the xlsx export.

SYMMETRIC_BAND is exercised only by a hand-constructed DeviationRule in tests/services/supplier/test_deviation_service.py:118; no SPEC_RULES entry carries that kind (M3). If the branch is meant to be reserved for a future rule, there is no test or comment marking it as such, so its status is ambiguous to the next reader.

The seed script's 'before' snapshot query has no test asserting it selects the same rows as apply_design_parameters' internal query (M8) — the two are kept in sync only by being textually identical today.
